title: Cloud SQL: PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server as a managed service

videos.script: Quitanda's orders live in PostgreSQL, on one server in a cupboard of the office. Somebody patches it when they remember. {{cupboard}} Cloud SQL is Google's offer to take that server away. The machine, the patches, the backups and the standby become Google's job. {{managed}} What stays yours is everything inside the database. The schema, the slow query, the missing index, the number of connections. And the bill. {{yours}} There is no Cloud SQL on your laptop, and no emulator for it. So you read the command that creates an instance, flag by flag, and nothing pretends to answer it. {{create}} Then you run the engine that Cloud SQL runs, PostgreSQL 16, on your own machine. You change two settings and watch one of them wait for a restart. {{flags}} That wait is the same on Cloud SQL, where a flag can restart your instance. {{restart}} And you price five instances for a month. The SQL Server one costs three times the PostgreSQL one on the same machine, and the licence is the difference. {{price}}
